core_obligations: Assume that the fibre of phi over zero is a single point and prove the nilpotence alternative. Restrict by rigidity to maps f: unit to x and g: unit to y out of the unit, and define the subcategory B_0 of finitely presented modules M for which there exists a non-zero compact z with the Yoneda module of z tensored with M equal to zero (source lines 896-899).

Show that B_0 is a Serre tensor-ideal, using that the compacts are local to prove closure under extensions, form the Gabriel quotient by B_0, and show that the maximal tensor-ideals of the quotient correspond exactly to the maximal tensor-ideals mapping to zero under phi: for every non-zero compact z the unit of the quotient embeds in the dual of z tensor z (source lines 900-904).

Under the hypothesis on the fibre, conclude that the quotient has a unique maximal Serre tensor-ideal, take the kernels M and N of the images of f and g, and show that if both Serre tensor-ideals they generate were proper then both would lie in the unique maximal one, so that the images of f and g in the further quotient would be monomorphisms into flat objects, making their tensor product a monomorphism and contradicting f tensor g = 0 (source line 904).

Prove the converse: assuming the nilpotence alternative, suppose that two different homological primes B and C lie in the fibre over zero, use that E_B tensor E_C = 0, factor the units of the two pure-injectives through compacts by finite presentability of the unit, apply the alternative to get nilpotence of one of them on a non-zero compact z, and deduce from the weak-ring property that E_B tensor z = 0, contradicting that the fibre over zero is reduced (source line 906).

proof_roadmap.step: Reduce to maps out of the unit and introduce the Serre tensor-ideal B_0 of modules killed by some non-zero compact.
Pass to the Gabriel quotient by B_0 and identify its maximal tensor-ideals with those in the fibre of zero.
Conclude the nilpotence alternative from the uniqueness of the maximal tensor-ideal of the quotient.
Conversely, rule out two homological primes over zero using E_B tensor E_C = 0, finite presentability and the weak-ring property.

difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the theorem at source lines 881-893, label Thm:hom-local, printed as Theorem A.1: for a big tt-category whose compact-rigid subcategory is local, the assertion that the fibre of the comparison map from the homological to the triangular spectrum over zero is a single point is equivalent to a nilpotence alternative, namely that whenever two maps f and g of compacts satisfy f tensor g = 0, one of them is tensor-nilpotent on some non-zero compact. The proof at source lines 895-907 constructs the bridge between the two statements rather than observing it: in one direction it builds the Serre tensor-ideal B_0 of finitely presented modules admitting a non-zero compact that kills them, verifies closure under extensions from locality of the compacts, passes to the Gabriel quotient, and proves that a maximal tensor-ideal of the quotient has zero preimage in the compacts exactly when it contains B_0, which uses the embedding of the quotient unit into the dual of a compact tensored with itself; then it shows that both kernels of f and g would have to be contained in the unique maximal tensor-ideal, forcing a monomorphism into a tensor product of flat objects and contradicting f tensor g = 0. The converse direction uses E_B tensor E_C = 0 for distinct homological primes, finite presentability of the unit to factor the units of the pure-injectives through compacts, and the weak-ring property to convert nilpotence into E_B tensor z = 0. Neither implication is a formal consequence of the definitions, and the appendix theorem is the paper's only unconditional characterization of injectivity of the comparison map.
